steps.title: Look at the two sentences.
steps.prompt: Why does the second sentence use the?
options: Because we already know which flat
steps.answer: Because we already know which flat
steps.why: a introduces something new. the points at something we already know.
steps.html:
I live in a flat.

The flat is on the 4th floor.

steps.title: a / an, the, and no article
steps.html:
UseWhenExample
a / anone thing, mentioned for the first timeThere's a fridge in the kitchen.
thewe both know which oneThe fridge is next to the window.
thethere is only onethe centre of the city, the East River
no articleplural or generalI like flats with big windows.
no articlecities, countries, streetsShe lives in Almaty, on Abay Street.

an goes before a vowel sound: an armchair, an old building.

The first time you name something, use a. After that, use the.

Learners often add the before plural general nouns. I like the flats means specific flats we both know.

steps.title: The ad
steps.html: FOR RENT: a bright studio flat in the city centre of New York. It's on the fourth floor of a quiet building, with a big window and a view of the city. The flat is cosy and modern, with a new fridge, a sofa and a shelf for your books. The neighbours are friendly. The rent is only $800 a month!

steps.title: The real flat
steps.html: I live in the flat from the ad. The photo was beautiful. The flat is… small. Very small. There is only one room: the kitchen, the sofa and the table are all in it. There isn't a cupboard. My bed is on a shelf above the kitchen. The building is opposite a garage, so the street is noisy at night. But the rent is $800, the view is great – and I don't want to move!
